question.worked_solution:
We must factor the quadratic expression

$$
20{b}^{2}-12b+1.
$$

First, we find two numbers that 

- multiply to the product of the quadratic coefficient and the constant ($20\times 1=20$), and

- add to the linear coefficient ($-12$).

Since the linear coefficient is negative and the product of the quadratic coefficient and constant is positive, we only need to consider the negative factor pairs of $20.$

The negative factor pairs of $20$ are

$$
(-1,-20),\,(-2,-10),\,(-4,-5).
$$

Notice the numbers in the factor pair $(-2,-10)$ add to $-12:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2)+(-10) & =-12\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we write the linear term as $-2b-10b,$ and factor the result by grouping:

$$
\begin{aligned}20{b}^{2}-12b+1 & = \\ 20{b}^{2}-2b-10b+1 & = \\ (20{b}^{2}-2b)-(10b-1) & = \\ 2b(10b-1)-(10b-1) & = \\ (2b-1)(10b-1) & \end{aligned}
$$
